thesis: Hold QQQ, IWM, and NVDA. Cash is $0, so any buy is a sale of one of those lines. The only hard fundamental is GameStop's 14% quarterly revenue rise and $2B buyback; other named ideas (AVGO ahead of earnings with no result in the title, FLNC soaring while helping Nvidia power data centers, an LLY buy-piece, CRDO, SMCI on Gorilla's $2B India deal, TFC, KNSL, NU, the UAL transcript, CNO, COST) have no open in the tape, so they are not ordered. NVDA is the listed name the pack still cites (Fluence helping Nvidia's data centers; the recycled nearly $20B five-month profit headline), which supports keeping that line rather than selling it. The same pre-open tape is two-sided on the AI book — Yahoo says stocks drop on AI and rate-hike worries as a Lebanon deal hits oil, plus a bitcoin liquidation crash and dotcom-bubble-2.0 fears, against continued data-center items — and the summaries are empty, so that mix does not justify liquidating QQQ into cash. No small-cap item against IWM. SpaceX's $1.75T IPO target is not a listed equity, and the SpaceX-or-Tesla June 12 comparison is not a TSLA order. The Iran-war gas headline and the Lebanon oil headline name no US equity; I will not invent XOM. House PTRs are filings only, with no tickers.
